sights.address: 130 Sutter St, San Francisco, CA 94104
sights.w: Willis Polk's 1918 seven-story wall of glass — believed to be the first American building with a glass curtain wall, and one of the city's most important architectural sights.
sights.k: Hallidie Building glass curtain wall Willis Polk

sights.address: 100 Larkin St, San Francisco, CA 94102
sights.w: Civic Center's 1996 Main Library by James Ingo Freed and Cathy Simon — a five-story skylit atrium crossed by bridges, and the San Francisco History Center on the 6th floor.
sights.k: San Francisco Main Library atrium History Center Civic Center

sights.address: 220 Montgomery St, San Francisco, CA 94104
sights.w: 1892 Financial District landmark that survived the 1906 earthquake — the last remaining West Coast example of the Chicago School; National Register and SF Landmark.
sights.k: Mills Building Chicago School Montgomery Street 1892

sights.address: Levi's Plaza, Battery St & Sansome St, San Francisco, CA 94111
sights.w: Lawrence Halprin's 1982 plaza at the foot of Telegraph Hill — a granite water garden and a Sierra-inspired 'soft' park; the Chronicle calls it the best park along the Embarcadero, all but hidden from sight.
sights.k: Levi's Plaza Lawrence Halprin fountain park

sights.address: 6210 Geary Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94121
sights.w: Outer Richmond landmark of the Russian Orthodox Church Outside Russia (built 1961–65) — five gold onion domes over Geary, heart of the Richmond's 'Little Russia'.
sights.k: Holy Virgin Cathedral Russian Orthodox onion domes Geary

sights.address: 2961 Webster St (at Filbert St), San Francisco, CA 94123
sights.w: 1905 Cow Hollow temple, the first Hindu temple in the Western world — a riot of towers: a crenellated castle turret, a Bengal-style double-bulb dome and a Taj Mahal dome over Moorish balconies; survived 1906 intact. View from the street.
sights.k: Old Vedanta Society Temple Cow Hollow first Hindu temple West

sights.address: Cottage Row (off Sutter St between Fillmore & Webster), San Francisco, CA 94115
sights.w: Hidden brick-paved lane of 1860s–70s William Hollis cottages (National Register district) by Japantown, with an Issei garden on the Sutter St frontage — Hoodline's 'secretly awesome' mini park.
sights.k: Cottage Row Mini Park Japantown Victorian cottages

sights.address: Salesforce Tower, Transbay (SoMa), San Francisco, CA 94105
sights.w: The city's tallest building (1,070 ft, 2018), crowned by Jim Campbell's 'Day for Night' — a nine-story LED video sculpture of street scenes, surf and sky, visible nightly from up to 20 miles away. Pairs with Salesforce Park next door.
sights.k: Salesforce Tower Day for Night Jim Campbell LED crown

sights.address: 140 New Montgomery St, San Francisco, CA 94105
sights.w: 1925 SoMa Art Deco tower, the city's tallest until 1927 — critics called it 'daringly original'; peek at the black-marble lobby with its stenciled ceiling and beaded gold-and-silver elevator doors.
sights.k: Pacific Telephone Building 140 New Montgomery art deco lobby

sights.address: 1067 Green St, San Francisco, CA 94133
sights.w: c.1857–58 Russian Hill octagon — one of only two surviving octagonal houses in SF, built in the phrenology-inspired octagon craze; private home, view from the street.
sights.k: Feusier Octagon House Russian Hill Green Street

sights.address: 236 Monterey Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94131
sights.w: 'The other conservatory' — a restored 1900 octagonal redwood glasshouse in a century-old palm grove and succulent garden, run by SF Rec & Park; survived six owners and the 1906 quake.
sights.k: Sunnyside Conservatory octagonal redwood glasshouse palm garden

sights.address: Cayuga Park, Cayuga Ave, Outer Mission/Excelsior, San Francisco, CA 94112
sights.w: Folk-art park where Rec & Park gardener Demetrio Braceros spent 20+ years carving hundreds of wooden figurines, totems and statues — angels, mermaids, knights and trolls — among themed gardens and trails.
sights.k: Cayuga Park Demetrio Braceros wood carvings folk art

sights.n: Spreckels Lake & SF Model Yacht Club
sights.address: Spreckels Lake, Golden Gate Park (north side), San Francisco, CA 94121
sights.w: Golden Gate Park lake built in 1904 purely for model boating — watch hobbyists sail from the WPA clubhouse of the San Francisco Model Yacht Club (1898), the oldest such club in the US.
sights.k: Spreckels Lake model yacht club Golden Gate Park

sights.address: Bush St, Polk Gulch, San Francisco, CA 94109
sights.w: 'Theatre of sound-sculptured space' operating since 1975 — up to 49 listeners sit in darkness inside sloping walls and a suspended ceiling of 176 speakers while a conductor moves the sound live; shows Thu–Sat, with guest residencies in 2026.
sights.k: Audium theatre of sound-sculptured space Polk Gulch

sights.address: 554 Fillmore St, San Francisco, CA 94117
sights.w: 19th-century Sacred Heart church turned roller-disco rink (2013) — skate under disco balls and stained glass while a DJ spins funk from a neon-lit altar; the building's history includes Black Panther free-breakfast programs.
sights.k: Church of 8 Wheels roller disco former Sacred Heart church

sights.address: Burlingame Caltrain station, Burlingame, CA 94010
sights.w: 1894 Southern Pacific depot — the first permanent building in the Mission Revival style, roofed with 18th-century tiles salvaged from Mission San Antonio de Padua and the San Mateo asistencia; a California Historical Landmark with a small train-station museum.
sights.k: Burlingame Railroad Station Mission Revival 1894 depot

sights.address: Milagra Ridge, off Sharp Park Rd, Pacifica, CA 94044
sights.w: 275-acre GGNRA ridge between Pacifica and Daly City — an easy 1.5-mile loop through coastal scrub with big ocean views.
sights.k: Milagra Ridge GGNRA Pacifica hike ocean views

sights.address: Gray Whale Cove State Beach, Highway 1 at Devil's Slide, CA 94038
sights.w: Half-moon cove of sand under high bluffs at Devil's Slide, south of Pacifica — breakers and a trail up to McNee Ranch's coastal ridge.
sights.k: Gray Whale Cove State Beach Devil's Slide

sights.address: 20th St & Church St (3899 20th St), San Francisco, CA 94114
sights.w: The hydrant at the top of Dolores Park credited with helping stop the 1906 fire — painted gold and ceremonially repainted every year at the corner of 20th & Church.
sights.k: Golden Fire Hydrant 1906 earthquake fire Dolores Park

sights.address: Wood Line, the Presidio, San Francisco, CA 94129
sights.w: A 1,200-ft serpentine line of eucalyptus branches through a Presidio grove (2010–11) — one of four Andy Goldsworthy land-art works here; his 90-ft cypress Spire stands near the Arguello Gate west of Inspiration Point.
sights.k: Andy Goldsworthy Wood Line Spire Presidio land art

sights.address: Warm Water Cove Park, east end of 24th St, Dogpatch, San Francisco, CA 94107
sights.w: Two-acre bayside pocket park at the end of 24th St, once the gritty 'Tire Beach' — picnic tables, trees and spring wildflowers facing the Bay, with sunset light on Oakland and Alameda.
sights.k: Warm Water Cove Park Tire Beach Dogpatch bay view

sights.address: Bayview Park, Bayview Hill, San Francisco, CA 94124
sights.w: Speakeasy of a park with one concealed entrance — a steep loop through grassland, woods and WPA-era stairs to near-360° views of downtown, the Bay and San Bruno Mountain; the Chronicle asks if it's SF's most underrated park.
sights.k: Bayview Park Bayview Hill hike 360 views
